(i) the structure of the emulsion is a major parameter affecting the kinetics of lipolysis and proteolysis during gastric digestion, (ii) the gastric digestion of infant formulas is affected by the aggregation of the proteins and (iii) the gastric digestion is affected by the surface specific area of the fat droplets.
the gastric digestion is a dynamic process that is affected by the structural properties of the milk emulsions.

understanding the role of the structure of emulsions (infant formula, breast milk) on their digestive (lipolysis and proteolysis) and structural kinetics and with determining the key parameters affecting the gastric digestion in the newborn.

the current knowledge of the impact of the structural features of the emulsions and their technological modifications on the digestion kinetics in the stomach is limited.
the current knowledge of the impact of food structure and digestion on infant health and disease is still in its infancy.
the current state-of-the-art in the area of food structure-function relationships in infant nutrition has to be considered as a promising but still very challenging field of research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gastric digestion of milk emulsions is highly dependent on their physico-chemical characteristics.
the gastric digestion of human milk is faster and more complete than that of infant formula.
the structure of the lipid phase in infant formulae and milk is important to consider in order to understand the impact of technological processes on the digestion of these matrices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many factors that affect gastric digestion, including the structure of the emulsion.
the composition of the infant formula has a significant impact on the digestion and the absorption of nutrients.
the structure of milk fat globule is a key factor in the digestion and absorption of lipids and proteins in infant nutrition.
